text:
If you’re hoping for a sunset, tonight looks like a washout: light rain is already hanging on, with steadier showers and an isolated rumble of thunder developing after 8. It’ll stay mild and muggy, near 67, but south winds will gust close to 30 mph. On the lake, a Wind Advisory is up, with 2 to 4 foot waves, so this is not an evening to linger on the water. Rain should ease toward daybreak, with roughly a quarter to half an inch possible overnight.

Tomorrow is the reset, mostly sunny with a high near 78 and a west wind gusting into the 20s. The forecasters favor a dry, brighter day, though the model spread is unusually wide on shower chances, so I’d keep a light rain layer handy rather than treat the sunshine as a lock. Plan on a damp, blustery night and a much better outdoor window Thursday, especially after the morning showers fade.
